tldr_label: TL;DR — Iran orders an 'unrestricted' response as reports point to US strikes after the midterms and a possible Doha breakthrough

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Mojtaba Khamenei ordered a 'geographically unrestricted' response to any attack. Reports say the US warned Gulf allies of strikes as early as November 4, while others report a possible breakthrough on direct talks in Doha. [[TAG:danger:strikes possible]]

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Thousands rallied in Tel Aviv for a Jewish-Arab coalition to remove Netanyahu, as Eisenkot weighs his options.

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Erdogan urged Russia and Ukraine to stop attacks in the Black Sea after meeting Zelensky in Istanbul. Evacuees from Oleshky reached Ukraine by way of Belarus.

tldr_bullets.label: Europe
tldr_bullets.body: About 320,000 people marched across France for a third weekend, and police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon. Youth-led protests are spreading across Europe.

tldr_bullets.label: Africa
tldr_bullets.body: Ebola deaths in DR Congo passed 5,000. The UN closed its political mission in Somalia, and its Western Sahara mission lapsed without renewal. [[TAG:danger:Ebola 5,026 dead]]

tldr_bullets.label: US vote
tldr_bullets.body: Trump reinstated Sunday rallies in Kansas and Iowa, where Senate races are toss-ups. Forecasters favor Democrats to win the Senate. [[TAG:info:vote Nov 3]]

sections.title: Iran: War or Talks
sections.summary: Khamenei orders an 'unrestricted' response as reports point to both strikes and Doha talks

paragraphs.heading: Khamenei's order
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel and ABC News (Australia) reported that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei told military chiefs to answer any attack with an 'immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response'. He also told commanders to update their target list to include all assets of the 'American-Zionist enemy'. The Jerusalem Post said the IRGC was told to respond immediately to any threat. Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said there will be no nuclear talks and Hormuz will not reopen until the US accepts Iran's demands, the Times of Israel reported. [[TAG:danger:escalation]]

paragraphs.heading: Strike warnings
paragraphs.body: Middle East Eye and Ynet, citing anonymous Gulf officials, reported that the US told Gulf allies to prepare for brief but intense strikes on Iran as early as November 4, the day after the midterms. Fox News reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump has not decided. ABC News reported Trump saying the US is not 'in a hurry' to agree a deal. All the reports rely on anonymous sources. [[TAG:warning:anonymous sources]]

paragraphs.heading: Doha channel
paragraphs.body: Ynet and The New Arab reported a 'breakthrough' in mediation by Qatar, with a US delegation expected in Doha for direct talks covering Iran's nuclear program, Hormuz and economic incentives. The Times of Israel and The Media Line carried the same reports. Iran's foreign minister denied there are plans to meet US officials, and Washington, Tehran and Doha have not confirmed any talks.

sections.sources: Times of Israel, ABC News (Australia), Jerusalem Post, Middle East Eye, Ynet, Fox News, ABC News, The New Arab, The Media Line

sections.title: Saudi Arabia Under Fire
sections.summary: Houthi attacks ground most flights at Riyadh's airport as Saudi air defenses are stretched

paragraphs.heading: Riyadh airport
paragraphs.body: Bloomberg reported that Houthi attacks on Riyadh's airport have driven up flight cancellations. Citing Cirium data, it said about 94% of departures were canceled from October 10 to 27. Al Jazeera examined whether the Houthis are using Russian satellites to target Saudi sites, and reported that missile strikes on the airport this month killed at least 12 people. [[TAG:warning:airport crippled]]

sections.title: Israel's Streets
sections.summary: Thousands rally for a Jewish-Arab coalition as Eisenkot sets out his terms

paragraphs.heading: Rallies
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and Haaretz reported that thousands gathered in Tel Aviv on Saturday to call for including Arab parties in a government that would remove Netanyahu, while his supporters held a counter-protest. Arab parties hold 19 of the Knesset's 120 seats.

paragraphs.heading: Eisenkot
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel live blog reported that Eisenkot will push for a state commission of inquiry, and that until a new government is sworn in he will support military operations only against direct and immediate threats. Herzog's consultations are expected next week. [[TAG:info:talks next week]]

sections.title: Ukraine
sections.summary: Erdogan presses both sides on Black Sea attacks; Oleshky evacuees reach Ukraine via Belarus

paragraphs.heading: Istanbul talks
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that Turkish President Erdogan urged Russia and Ukraine to stop attacks in the Black Sea after meeting Zelensky in Istanbul, and called attacks on civilian ships unacceptable. The Kyiv Post said the two leaders discussed peace talks and Black Sea security, and Zelensky said they agreed to work on a grain corridor.

paragraphs.heading: Strikes and evacuations
paragraphs.body: The Institute for the Study of War said Russia struck a combined heat and power plant in Kyiv and substations in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, while Ukraine hit a defense plant in Rostov and two refineries in Ufa. Al Jazeera reported that hundreds of evacuees from occupied Oleshky reached Ukraine by way of Belarus under the local truce. [[TAG:success:evacuations proceed]]

sections.title: Europe's Streets
sections.summary: France marches for a third weekend as youth-led protests spread across the continent

paragraphs.heading: France
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that the interior ministry counted about 320,000 protesters nationwide, with about 70,000 in Paris, and that police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon. Organizers claimed half a million. CBS News said the marches over the cost of living and schools were largely peaceful, with clashes in some cities. Arrest figures differ by time of report. Turnout fell from the previous weekend. [[TAG:warning:3rd weekend]]

paragraphs.heading: Across Europe
paragraphs.body: NPR reported that youth-led protests are spreading across Europe as France's unrest continues, with demonstrations planned in German cities and rallies in Poland and Albania.

sections.title: Africa and the UN
sections.summary: Ebola deaths top 5,000; UN ends its Somalia mission and lets the Western Sahara mandate lapse

paragraphs.heading: Ebola
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera, citing Congo's health ministry, reported that Ebola has killed 5,026 people out of 10,351 infected. The Washington Post and NBC News, carrying AP, reported growing fear that it will spread across the continent. The ECDC put deaths at 4,992 using data through October 28. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment. [[TAG:danger:5,026 deaths]]

paragraphs.heading: UN missions
paragraphs.body: UN News and Bloomberg reported that the UN's political mission in Somalia closed after three decades. The Washington Post said no replacement has been agreed to mediate Somalia's election dispute. CGTN reported that the Security Council failed to extend its Western Sahara mission. Accounts of the vote differ, so the details are unconfirmed. [[TAG:warning:vote details differ]]

sections.title: US Midterms
sections.summary: Trump reinstates Kansas and Iowa rallies as forecasters favor Democrats to win the Senate

paragraphs.heading: Final push
paragraphs.body: NBC News reported that Trump reinstated in-person rallies in Salina, Kansas, and Dubuque, Iowa, for Sunday after canceling them. Both states have Senate races rated as toss-ups. The Hill and Yahoo News reported the reversal, and CBS News said Trump also held online rallies.

paragraphs.heading: Forecasts
paragraphs.body: Poliwave's model gives Democrats about a 76% chance of winning the Senate, and PollCheck puts it at 66%. Kalshi's prediction market had Democrats at roughly 65% to 72%. These are forecasts, not results, and a 50-50 Senate would go to Republicans through the vice president's tie-breaking vote. [[TAG:info:forecasts only]]
